strategy.label: top-down model drafted from the report excerpt by the LLM pipeline (reverse-bafu draft)
strategy.note: basis: the chromic acid column of Tab. 44.3, whose Output row is 'anthraquinone kg 3000' - i.e. per 3000 kg of anthraquinone; allocation: none stated; 3 of 9 inputs carry a printed amount, 4 a printed range, 2 no number in the report (xxx Electricity, medium voltage, production UCTE, at grid, Chemical plant, organics). Review every derivation; unreviewed entries have reviewed_by = null.

gaps_reported_by_model: The dataset is an 80/20 average: 'an average process from the chromic acid process in Tab. 44.3 and the information at EMPA from the former studies is established - with an amount of 80% chromic acid process'. Only the chromic acid column is printed; 'the respective information from EMPA is not shown here due to confidentiality reasons'. The extracted list is therefore the 80 % share only.

The EMPA share contributes chlorobenzene (modelled as benzene + chlorine at 95 % yield) and aluminium chloride (modelled as aluminium + chlorine at 95 % yield). No amounts are given, so those four inputs are NOT included here.
The sulphuric acid amount actually used is 'the stoechiometric value based on an efficiency of 95%', which the report does not print.
Electricity, steam, infrastructure and both transports are named by the report but carry no numbers; they are free parameters for calibration.
The air emissions are given as percentage rules applied to inputs the report itself replaces, so their absolute values are uncertain.
'Due to confidentiality reasons, only the cumulated data from this dataset are available for the user of ...' - the dataset's own unit-process table is not published.
skipped_items: air (flow rate): ignore — Explicitly excluded by the report: 'The amount of air consumed is not shown in the ecoinvent dataset according to Frischknecht et al. (2007).' It is also a flow rate, not an amount per batch.

Sulphuric acid to air: no flow chosen (No candidate is airborne sulphuric acid or a sulfate aerosol. Sulfur Dioxide would be a different substance with a different formation route, and mapping sulphuric acid mist onto SO2 would be a substitution the report does not make. Reported as missing instead.)

naphthalene: ignore — Belongs to the naphthalene route, marked only with 'x' (no quantity). The report says 'this second source allows no quantification of the process in three of the four cases' and builds the dataset from the chromic acid column only.
xylene: ignore — Unquantified column of a route not used for this dataset.
butadiene: ignore — Unquantified column of a route not used for this dataset.
anthraquinone: product — Reference product; fixes the basis at 3000 kg.

node.name: Anthraquinone, at plant, disaggregated
node.comment: drafted from 2007 - LCI chemicals - Althaus.pdf pp. 445-447

inputs.name: Water, decarbonised, at plant
inputs.note: Printed value. The report does not say which water dataset is meant; low confidence on the mapping, not on the number.

derivation.quote: water   kg   9000   [Tab. 44.3 Input and output data for the production of anthraquinone, chromic acid column]
derivation.per: per 3000 kg anthraquinone (the 'chromic acid' column of Tab. 44.3, whose Output row is 'anthraquinone kg 3000')
derivation.mapping_reason: Process water for a chemical synthesis; decarbonised water is the standard ecoinvent chemical-process water, less treated (and so less committal) than completely softened or deionised water.

inputs.name: Chemicals organic, at plant
inputs.note: Printed value. The report maps it itself: 'the amount of anthracene used for the production of anthrachinone is shown in this study here as "chemiacal organics, unspecified"' because anthracene is not in ecoinvent.

derivation.per: per 3000 kg anthraquinone (the 'chromic acid' column of Tab. 44.3, whose Output row is 'anthraquinone kg 3000')
derivation.mapping_reason: The report itself states the anthracene input 'is shown in this study here as "chemiacal organics, unspecified"' because anthracene is not in the database; this is that proxy dataset.

inputs.name: Sulphuric acid, liquid, at plant
inputs.note: The report explicitly rejects this number: 'As then the above listed amount of sulphuric acid is not sufficient for the process equation, instead the stoechiometric value based on an efficiency of 95% is used here.' The stoichiometric value is not printed, so this is a bounded free input: raw_min is the printed 48 % active substance (4896 kg/3000 kg) and raw_max is a wide upper search bound chosen here, NOT a report value.

derivation.quote: sulphuric acid, 48%   kg   10200   [Tab. 44.3, chromic acid column]
derivation.per: per 3000 kg anthraquinone (the 'chromic acid' column of Tab. 44.3, whose Output row is 'anthraquinone kg 3000')
derivation.factor_source: the row is headed 'sulphuric acid, 48%' and the text says 'The input of sulphuric acid and of sodium dichromate is expressed as amount of active substance only', so x0.48 gives the active substance
derivation.mapping_reason: Purchased sulphuric acid at RER; the viscose by-product acid is a different source the report does not mention.

inputs.name: Sodium dichromate, at plant
inputs.note: Printed value, converted to active substance as the report states.

derivation.quote: sodium dichromate, 20%   kg   23500   [Tab. 44.3, chromic acid column]
derivation.per: per 3000 kg anthraquinone (the 'chromic acid' column of Tab. 44.3, whose Output row is 'anthraquinone kg 3000')
derivation.factor_source: the row is headed 'sodium dichromate, 20%' and the text says the input 'is expressed as amount of active substance only', so x0.20 gives the active substance
derivation.mapping_reason: Exact substance; every other candidate is a different sodium salt.

inputs.name: xxx Electricity, medium voltage, production UCTE, at grid
inputs.note: The input is named by the report but no amount is given for the chromic acid process ('In case of the chromic acid process no information about energy production is given. Therefore, it is assumed that the energy consumption is similar like in the other dataset.'). Entered as a free parameter with a wide search range; raw_value is a seed, not a report number.

derivation.quote: For the electricity consumed, an average European medium voltage mix (UCTE-mix) is used.
derivation.per: per 3000 kg anthraquinone (the 'chromic acid' column of Tab. 44.3, whose Output row is 'anthraquinone kg 3000')
derivation.mapping_reason: The report names 'electricity, medium voltage, production UCTE, at grid'; this candidate is that exact dataset at UCTE, beating the RER/CH grid mixes and the single-fuel UCTE variants.

inputs.name: Steam, for chemical processes, at plant
inputs.note: Named by the report, no amount given. Free parameter with a wide search range; raw_value is a seed, not a report number.

derivation.quote: The used steam is shown as "steam, for chemical processes, at plant (RER)" according to the description in Zah & Hischier (2007).
derivation.per: per 3000 kg anthraquinone (the 'chromic acid' column of Tab. 44.3, whose Output row is 'anthraquinone kg 3000')
derivation.mapping_reason: The only candidate and the exact dataset the report names.

inputs.name: Chemical plant, organics
inputs.note: Named by the report, no amount given. Free parameter; raw_value is a seed, not a report number.

derivation.quote: Concerning the infrastructure, due to a lack of more specific information, the module "chemical plant, organics (RER)" is used here.
derivation.per: per 3000 kg anthraquinone (the 'chromic acid' column of Tab. 44.3, whose Output row is 'anthraquinone kg 3000')
derivation.mapping_reason: The exact infrastructure module the report names.

inputs.name: Transport, freight, rail
inputs.note: The report says standard ecoinvent distances are used but prints none. Free parameter with a wide search range; raw_value is a seed, not a report number.

derivation.quote: Infrastructure and Transport: In the examined sources, no information about average transport distances for the raw materials used are indicated. Therefore, standard distances according to Frischknecht et al. (2007) are used within this dataset.
derivation.per: per 3000 kg anthraquinone (the 'chromic acid' column of Tab. 44.3, whose Output row is 'anthraquinone kg 3000')
derivation.mapping_reason: The report names 'transport, freight, rail' without a traction specification, which is exactly this RER average; the electricity-only and CH shunting variants are narrower.

inputs.name: Transport, freight, lorry, 16t-32t gross weight, fleet average
inputs.note: As for rail: named, not quantified. Free parameter; raw_value is a seed, not a report number.

derivation.quote: Infrastructure and Transport: ... standard distances according to Frischknecht et al. (2007) are used within this dataset.
derivation.per: per 3000 kg anthraquinone (the 'chromic acid' column of Tab. 44.3, whose Output row is 'anthraquinone kg 3000')
derivation.mapping_reason: The report names 'transport, lorry >16t, fleet average'; the 16t-32t RER fleet average is that dataset at the process's own location, beating the CH copy and the other weight classes.

emissions.name: Sulfate Ion
emissions.note: Printed per kg of product. Mapped to sulfate in water, the EF 3.1 flow that carries dissolved sulphuric acid.

derivation.quote: No removal efficiency for sulphuric acid was assumed, leading to emissions of 220 g sulphuric acid per kg product in the treated water.
derivation.per: per kg anthraquinone (value printed per kg product in the text of 44.4.1)
derivation.factor_source: g -> kg (x0.001) and then the table basis is 3000 kg of product while this value is printed 'per kg product'; x3000 puts it on the same basis (x3000): net factor 3.0
derivation.mapping_reason: Sulphuric acid released into treated wastewater is dissociated sulfate; the EF 3.1 sulfate ion in water is the closest available flow, and no undissociated sulphuric-acid water flow exists in the candidate list.

derivation.quote: The remaining amount of sodium dichromate is approximated by an emission of about 1 mol of sodium, e.g. 23 g/kg
derivation.per: per kg anthraquinone (value printed per kg product in the text of 44.4.1)
derivation.factor_source: g -> kg (x0.001) and then the table basis is 3000 kg of product while this value is printed 'per kg product'; x3000 puts it on the same basis (x3000): net factor 3.0
derivation.mapping_reason: The report says '1 mol of sodium' released in treated water, i.e. the dissolved ion; Sodium-24 is a radionuclide.

emissions.name: Chromium
emissions.note: Printed per kg of product. The report does not say whether this is Cr(III) or Cr(VI).

derivation.quote: and of 0.5 mol (due to a removal efficiency of 50%) of chromium ions, e.g. of 26 g/kg.
derivation.per: per kg anthraquinone (value printed per kg product in the text of 44.4.1)
derivation.factor_source: g -> kg (x0.001) and then the table basis is 3000 kg of product while this value is printed 'per kg product'; x3000 puts it on the same basis (x3000): net factor 3.0
derivation.mapping_reason: The report says 'chromium ions' without giving the oxidation state, so the unspecified chromium flow to water is correct; Chromium VI would assert a speciation the report does not state.

emissions.name: Chromium(6+)
emissions.note: Rule-derived, not printed as a number. Mapped to chromium VI because sodium dichromate is a Cr(VI) salt; low confidence on that mapping.

derivation.quote: and 0.2% of the sodium dichromate input (assumption);
derivation.per: per 3000 kg anthraquinone (the 'chromic acid' column of Tab. 44.3, whose Output row is 'anthraquinone kg 3000')
derivation.factor_source: 0.2 % of the sodium dichromate input (report rule) x 0.20 active substance (row header 'sodium dichromate, 20%'): 0.002 x 0.20 = 0.0004
derivation.mapping_reason: Sodium dichromate is a Cr(VI) salt and the report's air emission is that dust; Chromium(6+) to air is the matching speciated flow, while plain 'Chromium' to air would lose the hexavalent state the substance actually has.
